def: Cell-surface receptors activated by extracellular ATP or ADP. The P2Y12 subtype on platelets is the target of clopidogrel, prasugrel and ticagrelor, which block ADP-driven platelet aggregation.

Drugs that treat or prevent malaria by killing Plasmodium parasites at different life-cycle stages. Examples include chloroquine, primaquine (needed to clear liver hypnozoites) and artesunate; some, like primaquine, can cause hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.

Drugs that prevent or treat abnormal heart rhythms by changing ion channel function or autonomic input. Vaughan Williams classes are I sodium channel blockers, II beta blockers, III potassium channel blockers and IV calcium channel blockers.

A regular, fast atrial rhythm (about 300 beats per minute) from a re-entrant circuit, often around the tricuspid annulus. The ECG shows a sawtooth pattern of flutter waves, typically with 2:1 AV conduction.

A bruise of heart muscle caused by blunt chest trauma, such as a steering wheel impact. It can cause arrhythmias, conduction block or reduced pump function, and most often involves the right ventricle.

Drugs that block L-type calcium channels, lowering vascular tone and, for non-dihydropyridines, heart rate and AV conduction. Dihydropyridines (amlodipine, nifedipine) act mainly on vessels; verapamil and diltiazem act mainly on the heart.
An essential, branched-chain amino acid, along with leucine and valine. It cannot be made by the body, and its breakdown is impaired in maple syrup urine disease.

Salts containing the NO2- ion. They oxidize iron in hemoglobin to form methemoglobin, which is the basis of the nitrite step in cyanide poisoning treatment, and urine nitrite suggests bacteria that convert nitrate.
A breathing test that measures how much and how fast air is moved in and out of the lungs. It gives FEV1 and FVC and distinguishes obstructive from restrictive patterns.
The volume of air left in the lungs at the end of a normal quiet exhalation, where inward lung recoil balances outward chest wall recoil. It equals residual volume plus expiratory reserve volume.

An oxygen-binding protein in muscle with a single heme and a hyperbolic oxygen binding curve, so it holds oxygen more tightly than hemoglobin. Released from damaged muscle in rhabdomyolysis, it can injure the kidney.

Poisoning from inhaled carbon monoxide, which binds hemoglobin far more tightly than oxygen and shifts the curve left, impairing oxygen delivery. Causes headache, confusion and cherry-red skin; treat with 100% oxygen or hyperbaric oxygen.
Absence of hydrochloric acid in gastric secretions, seen in atrophic gastritis and pernicious anemia. Lack of acid raises gastrin levels and impairs iron and vitamin B12 absorption.
Benign, swollen outgrowths of inflamed nasal and sinus mucosa. Associated with chronic rhinosinusitis, asthma, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease and cystic fibrosis.
Gram-negative, obligate anaerobic rods that dominate the normal colon flora. B. fragilis causes intra-abdominal abscesses and is treated with metronidazole.
A beta-lactamase inhibitor given with ampicillin (Unasyn) to restore activity against beta-lactamase producing bacteria. It also has intrinsic activity against Acinetobacter.

Process in activated B cells that changes the antibody heavy-chain constant region (IgM to IgG, IgA or IgE) while keeping the same antigen specificity. Needs CD40-CD40L signaling and cytokines, and the enzyme AID.

CD4 helper T cell subset driven by IL-4 that secretes IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13. They promote B-cell IgE class switching and eosinophil activation, supporting defense against helminths and driving allergy and asthma.

Lung disease caused by Aspergillus, a mold with septate, acute-angle branching hyphae. Forms include aspergilloma in old cavities, allergic bronchopulmonary disease and invasive disease in neutropenic patients.
Targeted cancer drugs that block tyrosine kinase enzymes driving cell growth. Examples are imatinib for BCR-ABL in chronic myeloid leukemia and erlotinib for EGFR in lung cancer.
A light metal used in aerospace and electronics. Inhalation causes berylliosis, a chronic granulomatous lung disease that mimics sarcoidosis and raises lung cancer risk.
The thin serous membrane lining the lungs (visceral) and chest wall (parietal). The pleural space between them contains a small amount of fluid; parietal pleura is pain-sensitive.
Chronic lung disease of premature infants after prolonged oxygen and ventilator exposure, with impaired alveolar development. Defined by oxygen dependence at 36 weeks postmenstrual age.
A phosphodiesterase 3 inhibitor that raises cAMP, causing vasodilation and inhibiting platelets. Used for intermittent claudication; contraindicated in heart failure.
Inflammation of the colon with bloody, mucus-containing diarrhea, fever and cramps. Caused by Shigella, Entamoeba histolytica, Campylobacter and enteroinvasive E. coli.

A reactive oxygen species (O2 with an extra electron) produced by NADPH oxidase in the neutrophil respiratory burst. Converted to hydrogen peroxide by superoxide dismutase; absent production causes chronic granulomatous disease.

The active form of vitamin B1 and a cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase and transketolase. Deficiency causes beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy.
Vitamin B5, the precursor of coenzyme A and part of the fatty acid synthase acyl carrier. Deficiency is rare.
The mitochondrial pathway that oxidizes acetyl-CoA to CO2, producing NADH, FADH2 and GTP for oxidative phosphorylation. It starts with oxaloacetate combining with acetyl-CoA to form citrate.
A citric acid cycle intermediate formed from succinyl-CoA by succinyl-CoA synthetase and oxidized to fumarate by succinate dehydrogenase, which is also complex II of the electron transport chain.
Vitamin B7, a cofactor for carboxylase enzymes such as pyruvate carboxylase and acetyl-CoA carboxylase. Deficiency occurs with excessive raw egg white, whose avidin binds biotin.
A toxic intermediate of ethanol metabolism, made by alcohol dehydrogenase and broken down by aldehyde dehydrogenase. Its accumulation causes flushing and nausea, as with disulfiram.
Disorders that degenerate motor neurons, such as ALS, which involves both upper and lower motor neurons. Causes progressive weakness, atrophy, fasciculations and spasticity without sensory loss.

Defect in the diaphragm, usually left posterolateral (Bochdalek), letting abdominal organs enter the chest. It compresses the lungs, causing pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory distress in the newborn.

A glutamate receptor agonist that gives its name to the NMDA receptor, a ligand-gated ion channel permeable to calcium that requires glycine and depolarization to relieve magnesium block. Involved in long-term potentiation and excitotoxicity.
A cough suppressant that acts centrally and is an NMDA receptor antagonist. In high doses causes dissociative effects, and it can contribute to serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs.
A short-acting, competitive opioid receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses opioid overdose, including respiratory depression. Can precipitate withdrawal in dependent patients.
Communities of bacteria embedded in a self-made matrix and attached to a surface. They resist antibiotics and immune clearance, as on catheters, prosthetic valves, teeth and in cystic fibrosis lungs.
A fructose polymer that is freely filtered, not reabsorbed or secreted by the kidney. Its clearance gives an exact measure of glomerular filtration rate.

Three-layer barrier of fenestrated capillary endothelium, glomerular basement membrane and podocyte filtration slits. The negatively charged basement membrane restricts albumin and other anionic proteins.

Chronic optic neuropathy with raised intraocular pressure and an open drainage angle from impaired outflow through the trabecular meshwork. Gradually causes loss of peripheral vision and optic disc cupping.

Weight-loss operation creating a small stomach pouch connected directly to the jejunum, bypassing most of the stomach and duodenum. Risks include dumping syndrome and deficiencies of iron, B12 and calcium.

Autosomal recessive defect of the thick ascending limb (NKCC2, ROMK or ClC-Kb), mimicking chronic loop diuretic use. Causes hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, hypercalciuria and normal to low blood pressure.
A compound that shuttles long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for beta-oxidation via carnitine acyltransferases. Deficiency causes weakness, hypoketotic hypoglycemia and muscle problems.
An enzyme that converts dUMP to dTMP using methylene tetrahydrofolate, needed for DNA synthesis. Inhibited by 5-fluorouracil and, indirectly, methotrexate.
A dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor that acts against protozoa. Used with sulfadiazine to treat toxoplasmosis; folate deficiency is a toxicity, so leucovorin is added.
Uncoordinated movement and gait from cerebellar dysfunction, with wide-based gait, intention tremor and impaired balance. Lesions of the hemispheres cause ipsilateral limb signs.

Drugs that mimic or enhance sympathetic nervous system activity, directly stimulating adrenergic receptors or releasing norepinephrine. Examples are amphetamines, cocaine, pseudoephedrine and albuterol.
A selective central alpha-2A adrenergic agonist used for ADHD and sometimes hypertension. It reduces sympathetic outflow, causing sedation and low blood pressure.
A cardioselective beta-1 blocker with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity. Can cause drug-induced lupus.

Chronic inflammation causing loss of gastric glands. Autoimmune type affects the body and fundus and causes pernicious anemia with achlorhydria; environmental type involves the antrum and raises gastric cancer risk.
Antigen-presenting cells that capture antigen in tissues and travel to lymph nodes to activate naive T cells. They express high MHC class II and co-stimulatory molecules.
Proliferation of astrocytes in response to central nervous system injury, forming a glial scar. It is the main repair pattern in the brain since neurons rarely regenerate.
The cerebrospinal fluid-filled space between the arachnoid and pia mater, containing the major brain vessels. Subarachnoid hemorrhage bleeds into it.
The posterior gray matter of the spinal cord that receives sensory input from dorsal root fibers. Processes pain and temperature, relaying to the contralateral spinothalamic tract.
A midbrain nucleus that gives rise to the rubrospinal tract, which excites flexor muscles of the upper limb. Receives input from the cerebellum; lesions above it cause decorticate posturing.
Brief, visible twitching of muscle fibers from spontaneous firing of a motor unit. Seen with lower motor neuron disease such as ALS, and sometimes benign.
Cortical area in the postcentral gyrus of the parietal lobe that receives touch, proprioception and temperature input from the thalamus. Organized as a contralateral body map, the sensory homunculus.
Disorders of the cerebellum that cause ataxia, dysmetria, intention tremor and nystagmus on the same side as the lesion. Causes include stroke, alcohol, tumors and multiple sclerosis.
Myeloproliferative neoplasm with a sustained elevated platelet count, often with JAK2, CALR or MPL mutations. Causes thrombosis or bleeding and erythromelalgia.
Inflammation of the external ear canal, often from Pseudomonas, called swimmer's ear. Causes ear pain, especially with tugging on the pinna.
Main artery to the brain, ending as the anterior and middle cerebral arteries. Gives off the ophthalmic artery, and occlusion can cause amaurosis fugax.
Sudden painless monocular vision loss from blockage of the central retinal artery, usually by embolus. Retina is pale with a cherry-red spot at the fovea.
Neurodegenerative dementia with early behavior, personality or language changes and relatively preserved memory. Pick bodies (tau-positive) are classic in the behavioral variant.
Loss of normal REM muscle atonia so patients act out dreams, sometimes injuring themselves or a partner. A prodrome of alpha-synucleinopathies such as Parkinson disease and Lewy body dementia.
Severe watery diarrhea from Vibrio cholerae toxin, which activates adenylate cyclase via Gs and raises cAMP. Causes rice-water stools and dehydration; treated with fluid replacement.
Congenital blockage of a bowel segment from a vascular accident in utero. Jejunoileal atresia causes bilious vomiting and abdominal distention in the newborn.
Rare systemic infection by Tropheryma whipplei causing malabsorption, arthralgia and neurologic signs. Small bowel biopsy shows PAS-positive macrophages.
Autosomal dominant syndrome from APC gene mutation producing hundreds to thousands of colonic polyps. Colorectal cancer is nearly certain, so prophylactic colectomy is advised.
Delivery of nutrition into the gastrointestinal tract, by mouth or tube. Preferred over parenteral nutrition when the gut works because it preserves gut barrier function.
Obliteration of the extrahepatic bile ducts in infants, causing conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, pale stools and dark urine. Treated with Kasai procedure, often needing a later liver transplant.
Presence of gallstones in the gallbladder. Cholesterol stones are most common; risk factors include female sex, obesity and rapid weight loss.
An antiepileptic that binds synaptic vesicle protein SV2A. Used for focal and generalized seizures; side effects include irritability and mood changes.
Deep non-REM stage N3 with delta waves on EEG. Growth hormone is released here, and sleepwalking, night terrors and bedwetting occur in this stage.

Benign vascular tumor of proliferating endothelial cells. Infantile (strawberry) hemangiomas grow then regress, while cavernous hemangiomas have large vascular spaces and occur in the liver and brain.
IgE-mediated inflammation of the conjunctiva with itching, tearing and redness. Vernal keratoconjunctivitis is a severe form with giant cobblestone papillae.
A fluorescent dye used in the eye. Applied topically, it highlights corneal abrasions and herpetic dendrites under cobalt blue light; injected, it images retinal vessels.
A partial mu-opioid agonist with high receptor affinity and a ceiling effect on respiratory depression. Used for opioid use disorder; can precipitate withdrawal in patients on full agonists.
A serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor used for depression, anxiety, diabetic neuropathy and fibromyalgia.
Severe alcohol withdrawal with confusion, hallucinations, tremor, autonomic hyperactivity and fever, usually 2 to 4 days after the last drink. Treated with benzodiazepines.
A reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that crosses the blood-brain barrier. Used for anticholinergic toxicity.
Vaccine linking a polysaccharide antigen to a protein carrier so it engages T cells. This produces memory and strong responses in infants, as for H. influenzae type b and pneumococcus.
Malignant tumor of endothelial cells. Associated with vinyl chloride and arsenic exposure (liver) and with chronic lymphedema.
An antimalarial and immunomodulator used for lupus and rheumatoid arthritis. Can cause retinal toxicity; mild G6PD hemolysis risk.
IgM autoantibody against the Fc portion of IgG, found in rheumatoid arthritis. Not specific; anti-CCP is more specific.
Autoimmune disease causing skin thickening and fibrosis of internal organs. Limited type (CREST) has anti-centromere antibodies; diffuse has anti-Scl-70 antibodies.
Avascular necrosis of the femoral head in children aged 4 to 8, causing painless limp and hip or knee pain.
Fungal infection of the scalp and hair shafts, typically in children, with scaly patches of hair loss. Treated with oral griseofulvin or terbinafine.
A third-generation cephalosporin with good CSF penetration. Used for meningitis and gonorrhea.
A monoclonal antibody that blocks EGFR. Used for KRAS wild-type colorectal cancer and head and neck cancer; can cause acneiform rash.
Deep neck infection between the pharynx and prevertebral fascia, mostly in young children. Causes fever, neck stiffness and widening of prevertebral soft tissues on lateral x-ray.
Drugs that kill or slow cancer cells, including cytotoxic chemotherapy, hormonal agents and targeted drugs.
Plant-derived drugs vincristine and vinblastine that bind tubulin and block mitotic spindle formation. Vincristine causes neurotoxicity; vinblastine causes bone marrow suppression.
The C-shaped fibrocartilage cushion of the knee. The medial meniscus is attached to the MCL and torn more often.
A single round lung opacity under 3 cm. Calcification patterns suggest benign causes; growth suggests malignancy.
Lung infection acquired outside the hospital. Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common cause; atypical organisms include Mycoplasma.
Dimorphic fungus in the southwestern US causing coccidioidomycosis (Valley fever). Forms spherules with endospores in tissue.
An azole antifungal that inhibits ergosterol synthesis. Used for blastomycosis, histoplasmosis and sporotrichosis; inhibits CYP3A4.
Obligate intracellular bacterium spread by body lice causing epidemic typhus, with rash starting centrally and spreading outward.
Fungal infection of the nails, usually by dermatophytes, causing thick, discolored nails. Treated with oral terbinafine.
Spherical bacteria that stain purple on Gram stain. Staphylococci form clusters and streptococci form chains; catalase separates them.
Gram-negative coccobacillus causing tularemia, acquired from rabbits, ticks or deer flies. Causes ulceroglandular disease with fever.
A first-line tuberculosis drug that works in acidic phagolysosomes. Causes hyperuricemia and hepatotoxicity.
Presence of bacteria in urine. Asymptomatic bacteriuria is treated only in pregnancy or before urologic procedures.
Inflammation of the epididymis causing scrotal pain. Chlamydia and gonorrhea in young men; E. coli in older men.
Sebaceous glands in the eyelid tarsal plates that secrete the oily layer of tears. Blockage causes a chalazion.
A viral surface enzyme of influenza that cleaves sialic acid to release new virions. Inhibited by oseltamivir and zanamivir.
A non-enveloped RNA picornavirus spread by the fecal-oral route, causing acute hepatitis without chronic infection. Diagnosed by IgM anti-HAV.
A sulfonamide that inhibits folate synthesis. Used with pyrimethamine for toxoplasmosis; can cause crystalluria.
Malaria parasite causing benign tertian fever every 48 hours. Forms liver hypnozoites needing primaquine.
Family of bullet-shaped, enveloped, negative-sense RNA viruses including the rabies virus.
Biopsy using a wide-bore needle that removes a cylinder of tissue, preserving architecture for histology.
Precancerous abnormal squamous cells of the cervix from HPV, graded as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Detected by Pap smear.
A topical polyene antifungal that binds ergosterol. Used for oral and skin candidiasis; not absorbed.
Clumping of particles by antibodies. Used in blood typing, Coombs tests and latex tests.
Inflammation of the choroid and retina. Causes include toxoplasmosis, CMV and syphilis.
A peripheral mu-opioid agonist that slows gut motility. Treats diarrhea without central effects.
Medullary region at the floor of the fourth ventricle outside the blood-brain barrier. Triggers vomiting.
G-protein-coupled receptors. D1-like receptors raise cAMP; D2-like lower cAMP and are blocked by antipsychotics.
Rapid, irregular, involuntary dance-like movements. Seen in Huntington disease and Sydenham chorea after rheumatic fever.
Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor secreting VIP, causing watery diarrhea, hypokalemia and achlorhydria (WDHA).
Cytokines signaling between white blood cells, such as IL-1 for fever and IL-2 for T-cell growth.
Vitamin K-dependent cofactor of protein C, inactivating factors Va and VIIIa. Deficiency causes thrombophilia.
Precursor polypeptide cleaved into ACTH, MSH and beta-endorphin.
Dopamine D2 agonist used for prolactinoma, Parkinson disease and acromegaly.
Hypothalamic region for heat loss and sleep, including the preoptic area. Lesions cause hyperthermia.
Anterior pituitary hormone that stimulates thyroid hormone production. High in primary hypothyroidism.
Peptide cleaved from proinsulin and released with insulin. Low in type 1 diabetes and high with insulinoma.
Voltage difference across a cell membrane; the resting value is set mainly by K+ permeability, near -70 mV.
25-hydroxyvitamin D, made in liver and used to assess vitamin D status.
Low serum phosphate causing muscle weakness. Seen in refeeding syndrome and hyperparathyroidism.
Recurrent candida infections of skin, nails and mucous membranes from T-cell defects, such as AIRE.
Aggressive undifferentiated thyroid cancer in older adults, causing a rapidly growing neck mass. Very poor prognosis.
Inflammation of the aortic wall from syphilis, giant cell arteritis or Takayasu arteritis.
Cancer growing in finger-like projections. In the thyroid, Orphan Annie nuclei and psammoma bodies.
Inactive pancreatic precursor of trypsin, activated by enteropeptidase. Premature activation causes pancreatitis.
Enzyme converting glucose to sorbitol in the polyol pathway, contributing to diabetic cataracts and neuropathy.
Involuntary muscle spasms from low calcium, with Chvostek and Trousseau signs.
Nuclear receptors regulating lipid and glucose metabolism. Fibrates activate PPAR-alpha; glitazones PPAR-gamma.
Fibrous band from the uterus through the inguinal canal to the labia majora. Stretching causes pregnancy groin pain.
Intrauterine adhesions after curettage, causing amenorrhea or infertility.
Benign glandular tumor forming cysts, as in the ovary (serous or mucinous) or pancreas.
Surgical removal of the fallopian tube and ovary.
Abnormal placental attachment into the myometrium, causing hemorrhage at delivery. Increta and percreta are deeper.
Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets, a severe preeclampsia variant.
Prolonged painful erection unrelated to sexual stimulation; associated with sickle cell disease and trazodone.
Inflammation of the testis, classically from mumps virus.
Passage in the lower abdominal wall carrying the spermatic cord or round ligament.
Causes night blindness, xerophthalmia and Bitot spots.
Fluid-filled benign sac in the breast, common in fibrocystic change.
Benign growth in a breast duct, causing bloody nipple discharge.
Most common breast cancer, malignant ductal cells invading stroma.
Branch of the internal iliac supplying the uterus; the ureter passes beneath it ("water under the bridge").
Neural tube defect where the brain and skull vault fail to form; elevated AFP.
Phosphatidylcholine; the lecithin to sphingomyelin ratio assesses fetal lung maturity.
5-aminosalicylate anti-inflammatory used for ulcerative colitis.
Noncoding segments removed from RNA by splicing.
Antitumor antibiotic intercalating DNA. Used for Wilms tumor and rhabdomyosarcoma.
Transfer of ADP-ribose to proteins, as by cholera and diphtheria toxins.
Pancreatic protease cleaving after lysine and arginine.
Opioid and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor; lowers seizure threshold.
Prolonged ventricular repolarization risking torsades de pointes.
Liver failure and encephalopathy in children given aspirin during a viral illness.
ANCA-associated small vessel vasculitis; p-ANCA, no granulomas.
Nonatherosclerotic arterial disease with beaded renal arteries in young women.
Middle layer of artery wall of smooth muscle and elastin.
Potent IV vasodilator for hypertensive emergency; can cause cyanide toxicity.
Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker slowing AV conduction.
MI with elevated troponin and no ST elevation.
Contained rupture of artery wall where blood is held by outer tissue.
Cyanotic congenital heart disease with no tricuspid valve; needs ASD and VSD.
Period around childbirth, as peripartum cardiomyopathy.
Nonselective beta blocker with alpha-1 blocking effect, used in heart failure.
Lipid-laden foamy macrophage deposits in skin, seen in hyperlipidemia.
Pigment made by melanocytes from tyrosine; protects against UV.
Increased urinary sodium excretion.
Thiazide diuretic blocking NCC in the distal tubule; causes hypokalemia and hypercalcemia.
Main lymphatic vessel draining most of the body into the left venous angle.
Hemoglobin bound to carbon monoxide; reduces oxygen delivery.
Obesity with daytime hypercapnia.
Bacteria that grow without oxygen; abscess, foul smell. Treat with metronidazole.
Washing the distal airways with saline through a bronchoscope to sample cells.
Immune lung inflammation from inhaled organic dust, as in farmer's lung.
Tube placed in the pleural space to drain air or fluid.
Coagulation factor of the extrinsic pathway, shortest half-life; measured by PT.
Aldolase B deficiency causing hypoglycemia and vomiting after fructose.
Cofactor carrying acyl groups, derived from pantothenic acid.
Citric acid cycle intermediate between fumarate and oxaloacetate.
Glycosaminoglycan on cell surfaces; accumulates in Hurler and Hunter syndromes.
Devices turning liquid medication into a mist for inhalation.
Antidote for acetaminophen overdose; replenishes glutathione; mucolytic.
Fluid pressure in the eye; elevated in glaucoma.
Sulfur-containing amino acid forming disulfide bonds; cystinuria.
Nephrotic syndrome with scarring of parts of some glomeruli; common in Black patients and with HIV and heroin.
Kidney involvement in SLE; diffuse proliferative type is most common.
ENaC gain-of-function, causing hypertension, hypokalemia and low aldosterone.
Alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency (Hurler syndrome) with coarse facies and corneal clouding.
Nonprogressive motor disorder from early brain injury; spastic diplegia is common in preterm infants.
